subject: Cloudfolio contractual residency + retention SLA questions
messages:
From: Sonal Shah <sonal@cloudfolio.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marketplace Ops <marketplace@cloudfolio.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Residency + deletion process questions for Cloudfolio marketplace listing

Hi Laura —

Thanks for the onboarding call earlier. As we prepare the marketplace listing for Cloudfolio, procurement has a few specific questions we need to lock into the contract and the marketplace integration. High level asks:

1) If an end customer requests data deletion via the marketplace portal, who is the contractual owner of the deletion trigger? Cloudfolio (as the listing owner) or Redwood (as the service operator)?

2) What is Redwood's SLA for primary data erasure vs backups and snapshots? We need concrete windows to map into our T&C and procurement workflow.

3) Does Redwood replicate any customer inference artifacts (logs, prefixes, KV cache dumps) cross-region by default for durability? If so, what is the retention
period for those replicas and how are they deleted?

4) We need an explicit statement about egress/transfer behavior when data is moved between AWS/GCP/Azure regions for backup or replication. Any potential delays or manual approvals to be aware of?

Attached is a spreadsheet with the Cloudfolio environment mapping — can you annotate which buckets/regions Redwood will write to and the expected retention windows?

Appreciate a short write-up we can share with procurement/legal on your standard marketplace residency and deletion commitments. If easier, we can hop on a 30m call tomorrow.

Best,
Sonal
Sonal Shah
Head of Marketplace, Cloudfolio

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Residency + deletion process questions for Cloudfolio marketplace listing

Hi Sonal —

Thanks for the clear list. I pulled together the short write-up below; Ben and Priyom are looped in for sales/tech specifics. I also attached a first-pass SLA redline you can hand to procurement (CF-2026-031_SLA_draft_redlines.pdf).

Summary answers (high level):
- Deletion trigger ownership: Marketplace owners (Cloudfolio) can trigger deletions via the marketplace API or via a Redwood support ticket initiated by the listing owner. Operational execution is performed by Redwood under the contractual SLA.
- Primary data erasure SLA: Redwood will remove primary customer data within 7 calendar days of a validated deletion request (per agreement below).
- Backups/snapshots & replicas: Default backup/snapshot lifecycle is retained for 180 days; snapshots and cross-region backup replicas are removed per the backup retention window unless longer-term retention is explicitly requested and contracted.
- Cache/logs: Short-lived caches and KV artifacts are removed as part of background GC; logs are retained for 90 days for debugging and compliance reasons unless otherwise specified.
- Cross-region replication: Not performed by default for hosted marketplace listings in the "single-region" setup. Cross-region replication is an opt-in feature and will be called out in the listing and the SLA when enabled; it may incur additional data transfer/egress costs and could add 24–72 hrs to deletion propagation depending on replication topology.

Next steps: Ben will confirm marketplace-side workflow (who clicks what in the portal). Priyom will annotate the mapping sheet to show exact buckets and the tag/metadata we require to safely drive automated deletions. Marissa, if you have legal redlines on the windows above, please add.

--
Laura Bennett
Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Sonal — quick note from the marketplace / sales side:

- Marketplace deletion flow: Cloudfolio will be able to initiate deletion from the partner portal. That action creates a signed request we consume against a dedicated marketplace API endpoint. If Cloudfolio prefers, we can accept deletion via an authenticated support ticket as a fallback, but the portal flow is the preferred automated path.
- Contract mapping: The SLA Laura shared is what we put directly into the listing terms (we can mirror the same wording in our partner addendum). Procurement typically expects the 7-day primary erasure and the 180-day backup window called out — happy to show them the standard language.
- Egress: If Cloudfolio wants cross-cloud replication enabled (for DR), we will need to budget for egress and region-to-region transfer; we'll draft a note for procurement on estimated cost bands.

If helpful I can set up a 30-minute slot Monday with procurement and our legal ops to walk the redlines.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter | Strategic Partnerships — Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Residency + deletion process questions for Cloudfolio marketplace listing

Laura / Ben / Sonal —

Thanks for the draft. A few legal redlines and clarifications we'd like to propose for the partner addendum / listing terms:

1) Definitions: "Primary data" = data written to customer-designated object stores (S3/GCS/Blob) as a result of inference requests and attachments; "Backups/Snapshots" = managed point-in-time copies created by Redwood for recovery.

2) Deletion windows: Primary data to be erased within 7 calendar days of a validated deletion trigger. Cached runtime artifacts and non-authoritative replicas to be purged within 30 calendar days. Backups and point-in-time snapshots to be retained for a maximum of 180 calendar days unless a separate retention schedule is specified in writing.

3) Cross-region replication: If cross-region replication is enabled, Redwood will make best efforts to propagate deletion requests to replicas; however, deletion propagation time may be up to 14 calendar days depending on replication topology and third-party marketplace propagation delays. We will include a carve-out stating that extended propagation may be necessary where the replica is stored in a third-party-managed backup bucket.

4) Audit evidence: Redwood will provide deletion confirmation evidence (job IDs, object manifests) within 3 business days of completion. Copies of audit evidence will be retained for 12 months for compliance.

If Cloudfolio is good with the windows above I will incorporate them into the partner addendum. Sonal, please flag any procurement constraints.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Residency + deletion process questions for Cloudfolio marketplace listing

Thanks — technical confirm and mapping notes below (annotating the spreadsheet rows):

- Bucket placement: For a single-region marketplace listing we will write to the customer-designated bucket in the chosen region (naming example: redwood-marketplace-us-west-2/cloudfolio/<customer-id>/). The exact bucket path and object prefix will be added to the sheet (see cloudfolio-residency-mapping.xlsx).
- Deletion pipeline: When Cloudfolio triggers a deletion via the marketplace API we expect a signed payload. That creates a deletion job in our queue which: 1) marks the dataset as "deleting", 2) removes primary objects via S3/GCS/Azure API calls (we target completion within 48 hours for primary objects), 3) enqueues background GC for caches (expected 72 hours), and 4) schedules snapshot/backups for deletion according to the contract (default 180 days).
- Replicas: We do not create cross-cloud replicas by default. If Cloudfolio opts into cross-region replication, we will create a replication set and store replica metadata with a delete_on tag; our pipeline tries to coordinate deletion across replicas but cannot force deletion in third-party-managed marketplace buckets — that can add up to 14 days as Marissa notes.
- Evidence: Our deletion job emits a manifest listing deleted object keys and a job ID. We can deliver the manifest (CSV) via secure Drive link or HubSpot attachment per Cloudfolio preference.

I'll upload my annotated spreadsheet to the Drive link and flag the exact prefixes for procurement.

—Priyom
Principal Engineer, Integrations — Redwood Inference
